Two call sites, not three. That's the Rule of Three threshold not met yet — I'd name it and let it sit rather than build the helper now.

Reasoning: with only two instances you're guessing at the shape of the abstraction — what varies between the two (max retries, backoff base, which exceptions are retryable, jitter or not) isn't enough data yet to know what the helper's actual interface should look like. Build it now and you're likely to either overfit to these two call sites or over-generalize params you don't have evidence for yet.

What I'd actually do: note it in passing — "retry-with-backoff duplicated at X and Y, watching for a third" — and move on. If a third call site shows up, that's when I'd write the plan for a shared helper, and at that point I'd want to look at all three sites together to figure out what's actually common versus what's incidental.

If there's a reason this pair is higher-stakes than usual — e.g. the two implementations have already drifted and one has a bug the other doesn't — that's a different conversation (a correctness bug, not a duplication call). Is that what's actually prompting this, or just noticing the repeat?
